items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: It turned out we got Joe Grasso. ... Joe Grasso had a disc recorder of some sort. ... And while he was playing drums, he would operate this thing.

ctx.x: Child's, was that like a cafeteria?

That was a cafeteria, and this was 1940. I'd been in New York practically two years, and so I said, sure. He says, okay, who would you like to have? I says, well, I'd like to have George Brunis who's available, I'd like to have Rod Clers Ron -- less. I don't know who I can get on drums. It turned out we got Joe Grasso. And on trumpet, I couldn't get Marty Marsala : he wasn't available. And I didn't know about I never I hadn't felt that scene yet.
